summary: In Greek mythology, Bias (Ancient Greek Βίας) is an Athenian warrior who follows Menestheus son of Peteos among the picked Athenians at the ships in Iliad 13, with Pheidas and Stichius, when the battle cries unquenchable against Hector's press. Distinct from Bias of Pylos, Bias son of Amythaon, the Trojan Bias, and the Dulichian suitor.
etymology: Ancient Greek Βίας; this node is fixed by Menestheus' Athenian company in Iliad 13, not by the bare name.

sections.heading: With Menestheus at the ships
paragraphs: Homer names Menestheus son of Peteos as leader of the picked Athenians, and there follow Pheidas, Stichius, and valiant Bias when the fight rages at the foremost ships (Iliad 13). Wikipedia's Bias (mythology) entry records him as an Athenian soldier who supported Menestheus against Hector's attacks.
The atlas id bias-athenian is that Homeric Athenian alone; he receives no further myth outside the Iliadic muster.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: Not bias-pylian (Nestor's shepherd of the host); not bias-aeolid (Amythaon's Argive king); not bias-trojan (father of Laogonus and Dardanus); not bias-dulichium (Penelope's suitor). The shared Wikipedia disambiguation also lists a Megarian Bias son of Lelex.
